channel.title: Ajahn Funn Ācāro Quotes
channel.description: Dhamma quotes by Ajahn Funn Ācāro, updated every 24 hours

item.title: Ajahn Funn: So concentration is a mind firmly established. Discernment is all-around knowledge of the affairs of fabrication (saṅkhāra). And what is it that fabricates,…
item.description:
Discernment: All-Around Knowledge of Fabrication

So concentration is a mind firmly established. Discernment is all-around knowledge of the affairs of fabrication (saṅkhāra). And what is it that fabricates, that gives rise to becoming and birth? To kamma, animosity, and danger? What is it that goes to these things? We’re the ones who give rise to them. That’s what discernment sees. You need all-around knowledge of fabrication for it to count as discernment. The problem is that we’re deluded by fabrication. That’s why there’s so much trouble and suffering as we build up becoming and birth, build up kamma, animosity, and all kinds of dangers.

So when you hear this, opanayiko—bring it inwards and ask yourself: Is this what you want, all this death? Is there anyone who really wants it? Nobody at all. We don’t want to be sick without any doctors or medicine. And yet we keep nourishing these things that belong to Māra: the Māras of the aggregates, the Māras of defilement, the Māras of mental fabrications, the Māras of death. No matter how much we try to nourish and protect them, they don’t lie under anyone’s control—for anyone at all. That’s the way things are.

item.title: Ajahn Funn: Now, upāsakas and upāsikās should observe the five precepts. Do not kill buffalo or cattle. Do not think that the precepts are received…
item.description:
The Five Precepts Are Complete Since Birth: Two Legs, Two Arms, One Head

Now, upāsakas and upāsikās should observe the five precepts. Do not kill buffalo or cattle. Do not think that the precepts are received from the monks. The precepts are with the monks? The monk says the precepts are with the Buddha. The religion is with the Buddha. If we do not consider them as our own, we become discouraged and disheartened. If we consider them as our own, we pay attention. With whom else would we receive them?

The five precepts – I will explain. We have had them complete since birth: two legs, two arms, one head – that’s five. This is the body of the five precepts. Then do not use these five to commit the five wrongdoings. What are the five wrongdoings? Pāṇātipāta – that is a wrong. Adinnādāna – that is a wrong. Kāmesu micchācāra – that is a wrong. Musāvāda – that is a wrong. Surāmeraya – that is a wrong. All are wrongdoings. The troubles we have today are because of this. We fear being killed, fear thieves, fear sexual misconduct, fear lying, cheating, deceiving, fear drunkenness – alcohol, drugs, opium. These are the wrongdoings. If we refrain from these, He said: sīlena sugatiṃ yanti – they go to a happy state. Sīlena bhogasampadā – there is achievement of wealth. Understand this.

item.title: Ajahn Funn: This is how we will know whether the religion is declining or prospering. How does the religion decline? It is when our mind…
item.description:
Virtue Is the Core of Buddhism: Beautiful in the Beginning, Middle, and End

This is how we will know whether the religion is declining or prospering. How does the religion decline? It is when our mind does not develop the iddhipāda (paths of accomplishment) and does not develop virtue (sīla), concentration (samādhi), and wisdom (paññā), which are the core of Buddhism. This is how it is. Virtue is the core of Buddhism. Look: what is virtue? In the Pāli it is said: ādikalyāṇaṃ, majjhekalyāṇaṃ, pariyosānakalyāṇaṃ.

Kalyāṇa means beauty – beautiful in the beginning, beautiful in the middle, beautiful in the end. What is beautiful in the beginning? Being a person of virtue. What is virtue? He said: restrain body, speech, and mind to be orderly. Look: our body is orderly, our speech is orderly, our mind is orderly. We have not committed any wrong, great or small, through body or mind. Then we are a person of virtue.

Sīla means normalcy of body and mind. Right now, is our mind normal? If it is normal, what is it like? It is not distorted, not agitated. Our body is normal, not distorted. Contemplate this: make the mind normal. Sila is like a stone. Like a rock: when the wind blows from all four directions, it does not tremble. Now we make the mind like a rock. No matter what anyone says, good or bad – it does not become what they say.

item.title: Ajahn Funn: Opana-yiko – we must bring it inward. Paccattaṃ – to be known only by oneself. Who is it that knows feeling? Who knows…
item.description:
Bring It Inward: Who Says "Earth Element"? – The Knower Remains

Opana-yiko – we must bring it inward. Paccattaṃ – to be known only by oneself. Who is it that knows feeling? Who knows perception? Who knows formations? Who knows consciousness? We must bring it inward. Who says "earth element"? Who says "water element"? Who says "wind element" and "fire element"? One who is not awakened (puthujjana) does not know anything. When we analyze and separate them out, what remains is the Buddha – the Knower. Thus we grasp the matter. Not knowing anything is because things are obscured. One doesn't know what to take as happiness, what to take as suffering, what is good, what is bad – it's dark like that. Now, we have analyzed. Whatever part is earth element, it becomes earth. Whatever part is water element, it becomes water. Whatever part is wind element, it becomes wind. Whatever part is fire element, we see it all as fire. What is fire? What is earth? Does it sleep? Does it lie down? Does it get sick, feel pain, get tired, get hungry? We contemplate these things to know, in order to eliminate danger, eliminate enmity, eliminate defilements, craving, lust, greed, hatred, delusion, ignorance, craving, attachment, becoming, birth. Then we will not cling or grasp.

item.title: Ajahn Funn: Now, I have explained both external and internal. So, turn inward. Now, where do these things come from? Let us all abstain, let…
item.description:
Measuring the Mind: Where Is It Stuck? Fix It Right There

Now, I have explained both external and internal. So, turn inward. Now, where do these things come from? Let us all abstain, let us know. Now, from this point on, set your mind to look, focus right now. Where are the wrongdoings? Where is happiness? Where is suffering? Let us all know and understand. Where is our country troubled? Just like building a road: wherever there is an obstacle, we fix it. This mind of ours: where is it stuck? Where is it caught? We fix that. It’s not about sitting with eyes closed, just getting a sore back for no reason. We sit and look at ourselves. Right now, what level are we in? What plane of existence? Know your mind: is it wholesome or unwholesome? Know it. Is our mind calm or not? Is our mind good or not? Know this: kāmāvacaraṃ kusalaṃ cittaṃ – know our own mind. Uppannaṃ hoti – it arises from our own self. Now, from now on, each one of you, opanayiko – turn inward and look. This is it: contemplate, focus on our own heart. What are we attached to? What is our mind like? Our mind good – what is it like? Our mind good is like this: the mind is calm and good, it has happiness, ease, coolness of heart, no suffering, no fever, no turmoil, no disturbance. Buddho – the heart is cheerful, at ease. This is a good mind, bringing happiness and prosperity in the present and the future.

item.title: Ajahn Funn: So turn and look at consciousness. What level is it on? Watch it to see if it’s on the level of sensuality, the…
item.description:
Watching Consciousness: From Sensuality to Formlessness to Unbinding

So turn and look at consciousness. What level is it on? Watch it to see if it’s on the level of sensuality, the level of form, or the level of formlessness. The level of sensuality is where it travels around in sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and tactile sensations. These come in two sorts. When the mind is unskillful, it’s on the levels of deprivation. When the mind is clear and bright, it’s on the levels of the six sensual heavens. I’ve already explained these things in the past. No matter what the level, wherever there’s birth, aging, illness, and death, then there’s suffering and stress.

So focus on the level of form. Don’t send the mind anywhere else. When you see that the form of the body has no essence to it, you can let it go. When you let go of form, there’s nothing left but formlessness, nothing left but the mind at one: That’s the level of the Brahmās. Everything is empty. When you see that that’s true, you realize that it, too, has no essence to it. It’s inconstant. That’s when you can be done with it. When you see that all levels of becoming are inconstant, that’s when you can go to unbinding.

item.title: Ajahn Funn: Let us all pay homage every day. After paying homage, go to the monastery. Look at the Buddha-refuge of ours, the Dhamma-refuge of…
item.description:
Going to the Monastery: Looking at Our Own Mind

Let us all pay homage every day. After paying homage, go to the monastery. Look at the Buddha-refuge of ours, the Dhamma-refuge of ours, the Saṅgha-refuge of ours. Then go to the monastery. Do we yet know the monastery? Nowadays people do not know the monastery, which is why they are troubled and distressed. If each person went to the monastery, there would be no trouble. What monastery? The monastery of looking at ourselves. It is not the monastery of the Buddha or the monks. Our monastery is present in everyone every day. Pay homage to the Buddha, Dhamma, and Saṅgha three times. Then sit and look at our own mind. Recollect the Buddha within the mind, the Dhamma within the mind, the Noble Saṅgha disciples within the mind. Recite the meditation words: buddho, dhammo, saṅgho three times, then gather into one: buddho alone in our mind. Our mind focuses on buddho, buddho. Close your eyes, close your mouth, recollect within the mind. The tongue does not move. Our mind focuses on the recollection buddho. Our ears listen to the recollection buddho. Buddha means the one who knows. Focus on knowing why we are born and suffer, why we are happy, where suffering is, where happiness is. The Buddha thus established buddha as the one who knows. This is our refuge.

item.title: Ajahn Funn: Now, we see the suffering and danger in saṅkhārā — the suffering and danger of saṅkhārā is birth, aging, sickness, death. Having seen…
item.description:
When There Are No More Saṅkhārā, Birth, Aging, Sickness, Death No Longer Exist

Now, we see the suffering and danger in saṅkhārā — the suffering and danger of saṅkhārā is birth, aging, sickness, death. Having seen the danger and peril of this cycle of existence (saṃsāra), then we cease those very saṅkhārā.

When there are no more saṅkhārā, then birth, aging, sickness, and death no longer exist. All sufferings no longer exist. What could cause suffering? There is no concocting, no fabricating; it is peaceful. Our mind is calm and still within. It does not create realms or births (bhave bhavā sambhavanti — small realms, great realms). It doesn’t go there. It remains still, one thing only. It sees only purity. It does not send itself forward or backward, left or right, past or future. It is fixed on one place only. Knowing is not something that breaks, is destroyed, becomes nothing, or disappears. It just knows like that. It is amataṅ — the deathless. It does not die, is not destroyed. It remains everlasting, permanent. Freedom from suffering is right there. Not free anywhere else. Free right at that knowing place. Why is it free from suffering? The mind is not suffering, so there is nothing to suffer. It is still. It does not conceive or assume. It doesn’t say “good,” it doesn’t say “bad,” it doesn’t say “suffering,” it doesn’t say “pleasure,” it doesn’t say “right,” it doesn’t say “wrong.” It doesn’t say anything at all.

item.title: Ajahn Funn: The ānisaṃsa of observing precepts is the restraint of body, speech, and mind to make them proper. When we no longer commit any…
item.description:
The Ānisaṃsa of Observing Precepts: Freedom from Danger and Faults

The ānisaṃsa of observing precepts is the restraint of body, speech, and mind to make them proper. When we no longer commit any wrongdoings, great or small, with body or mind, then in whatever birth or realm we are born, we become people with complete bodies, beautiful and handsome, without disease or danger, without depravity or corruption. Because we have restrained and guarded ourselves – our bodies are proper, our speech is proper, with no faults great or small – then we are complete people. Wherever we go, there is no danger, no enemies, no evil. As laypeople, our basic precepts are the five precepts. From the moment we are born from our mother’s womb, we already have the five precepts with us. What are they? Our two legs – that’s two; our two arms – that makes four; and the head – that’s the fifth. They are all present from birth, namely the five precepts themselves. When we have these five precepts, we abstain from the five faults.

Why do we abstain from the five faults? Pāṇa – that is a fault. Adinna – that is a fault. Kāme – that is a fault. Musā – that is a fault. Surā – that is a fault. They are all faults. No one wants or desires these five things. The trouble and difficulty we have today are precisely because of these five things – people do not abstain from them.

item.title: Ajahn Funn: We have come to this meeting – meeting both internally and externally. Having arrived at the monastery, let us all measure and observe…
item.description:
The Religion Flourishes or Declines Depending on Our Respect for Seven Things

We have come to this meeting – meeting both internally and externally. Having arrived at the monastery, let us all measure and observe our own minds. Is it inside the monastery or outside? For what purpose are we measuring? This very point: we rely on Buddhism. This religion is a tool for alleviating suffering and extinguishing suffering.

The Buddha established the religion within the four assemblies – right here, not elsewhere. What are the four assemblies? Bhikkhus, bhikkhunīs – but at present there are no bhikkhunīs, only bhikkhus, sāmaṇeras, upāsakas, and upāsikās. The religion flourishes depending on these four; the religion declines depending on these four. Why does it decline? Because we do not conduct ourselves or practice in line with the qualities of the Buddha. We have no respect for the qualities of the Buddha, no respect for the qualities of the Dhamma, no respect for the qualities of the Noble Saṅgha, no respect for giving, no respect for virtue, no respect for meditation, no respect for mutual courtesy and hospitality. When we lack respect for these seven things, that causes the religion to decline. If we still have respect for these seven things, the religion will prosper and advance.
